Recall:
 \[\frac{d}{d{{CT:2}}}\left(\frac{1}{{{CT:2}}^{\frac{1}{{CT:3}}}}+{{CT:4}}\right)=\frac{d}{d{{CT:5}}}\left(\frac{1}{{{CT:2}}^{\frac{1}{{CT:3}}}}\right)+\frac{d}{d{{CT:5}}}\left({{CT:4}}\right).\]

 Now remember that the differential of a constant is \(0\). So we need to find: \[\frac{d}{d{{CT:2}}}\left(\frac{1}{{{CT:2}}^{\frac{1}{{CT:3}}}}\right).\]

 Using the laws of indices this is: \[\frac{d}{d{{CT:2}}}\left({{CT:2}}^{-\frac{1}{{CT:3}}}\right).\]

 We can now apply the standard rules of differentiation to get:

 \[\frac{d}{d{{CT:2}}}\left({{CT:2}}^{-\frac{1}{{CT:3}}}\right)=-\frac{1}{{CT:3}}{{CT:2}}^{{CT:6}}=-\frac{1}{{{CT:3}}\cdot{{CT:2}}^{{CT:7}}}.\]
